For projection predicates, it calls `deduce_sig_from_projection` and normalizes the result, then filters out self-referential inferred signatures using the local `MentionsTy::visit_ty` visitor; it also derives closure kind information from encountered Fn-trait predicates.

Extracts an expected function signature from a projection predicate on an `Fn*` trait or coroutine `Return` associated type. It validates that the projection comes from a supported trait, resolves tuple inputs and return type, and constructs the resulting `ExpectedSig`.

Chooses how to compute a closure signature based on whether an expectation is available. It calls `sig_of_closure_with_expectation` when an expected signature exists, otherwise it calls `sig_of_closure_no_expectation`.

Computes closure signatures without contextual expectations. It calls `supplied_sig_of_closure` to obtain the user-declared or inferred poly-signature, then calls `closure_sigs` to derive the bound and liberated forms.

Handles the case where the expected signature and closure declaration have different arities. related_methods.reason: This is the main coroutine/closure type-checking path. It builds the concrete coroutine type, invokes `check_fn` on the coroutine body, and wires in coroutine typing information such as yields/interior types. Since the bug is that `yield ()` inside a coroutine body is effectively accepted as `Invariant<'b>` instead of the expected resume type `Invariant<'a>`, the logic here is highly suspicious because it mediates the body signature used for checking and the final `ty::Coroutine` construction.

The reproducer relies on contextual typing from `fn x<'a, 'b>() -> impl Coroutine<Invariant<'a>>`, so the coroutine literal is checked with an expected `Coroutine` signature derived from the return-position `impl Trait`. This method incorporates expectation-derived signatures into closure/coroutine checking and can fall back when merging fails.
